:::{#thm-binomial-sum-bernoulli}
#### A sum of IID Bernoulli variables is binomial

If $\dsn{X}$ are [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) $\Ber(\prob)$ random variables,
then their sum $S = \sumin X_i$ has the $\dBinf{n, \prob}$ distribution.

:::

::: proof

Each $X_i$ is $0$ or $1$, so $S$ takes values in $\set{0, 1, \dots, n}$.
Let $x \in \set{0, 1, \dots, n}$ be a value of $S$,
and let $A_x$ be the set of sequences $(\dsn{s}) \in \set{0, 1}^n$
with exactly $x$ ones.
The event $\set{S = x}$ is the disjoint union of the events
$\set{X_1 = s_1, \ldots, X_n = s_n}$ over $(\dsn{s}) \in A_x$.
For one such sequence:

$$
\ba
\P(X_1 = s_1, \ldots, X_n = s_n)
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \P(X_i = s_i)
&& \text{(independence)} \\
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \prob^{s_i} (1 - \prob)^{1 - s_i}
&& \text{(Bernoulli PMF)} \\
&= \prob^{\sumin s_i} (1 - \prob)^{\sumin (1 - s_i)}
&& \text{(collect exponents)} \\
&= \prob^x (1 - \prob)^{n - x}
&& \text{(} \textstyle\sumin s_i = x \text{ for a sequence in } A_x \text{)}
\ea
$$

Choosing which $x$ of the $n$ positions hold the ones
determines the sequence,
so $A_x$ has $\binom{n}{x}$ elements.
Therefore:

$$
\ba
\P(S = x)
&= \sum_{(\dsn{s}) \in A_x} \P(X_1 = s_1, \ldots, X_n = s_n)
&& \text{(additivity over disjoint events)} \\
&= \sum_{(\dsn{s}) \in A_x} \prob^x (1 - \prob)^{n - x}
&& \text{(probability of one sequence)} \\
&= \binom{n}{x} \prob^x (1 - \prob)^{n - x}
&& \text{(} A_x \text{ has } \tbinom{n}{x} \text{ elements)}
\ea
$$

which is @eq-binom-pmf.

:::
